correctness.rationale: For any input positive contraction, the distinguished diagonal of Γ−Γ² gives ||z||²≤p(1−p). The two output Schur complements for 0<p<1 are B−η²z*z/p and I−B−η²z*z/(1−p). Both are positive semidefinite under the claimed bound; p=0 or 1 forces z=0. For necessity use the rank-one projection onto (√p,√(1−p)v). Taking expectations in v and sending p toward 0 or 1 recovers the respective lower and upper Rayleigh bounds, without requiring an eigenvector. Schur complementing the bath blocks instead gives the fixed-input formula when both are boundedly invertible. Decreasing thermal functional calculus gives the energy-edge formula; independent substitution at βJ=3, μ=0 gives 0.04972547794274857. In the system-first occupation basis the cross observable has a system parity factor and one bath raising/lowering operator, so the identity-on-system times the stated qubit map scales its expectation by η. The trace-preserving Choi matrix has one nontrivial block with diagonal (1−c,c) and off-diagonal η, giving the distinct local CP threshold.
residual_risks: The local implementation statement is restricted to the indicated one-mode channel and second moments, not general many-body or multimode implementations. The uniform theorem does not classify particular trajectories.

originality.rationale: The reset itself and the phase-covariant qubit CP inequality are prior work. The supported distinct claim is the sharp all-input spectral covariance threshold for this reset, including non-eigenvalue bath edges, and its contrast with the prior local-channel criterion. Neither the exact model passages nor the broader reset or channel results inspected establish that uniform condition. This is a bounded best-of-knowledge conclusion.
residual_risks: Other work on affine covariance maps or on this reset may contain an unlocated equivalent uniform criterion. There is no claim of priority for standard Schur tests, thermal spectral mapping, or the one-mode CP inequality.

value.rationale: The cutoff addresses a physical admissibility question in a previously proposed, explicitly parameterized reset. The thermal example shows how small a portion of its nominal parameter range can have a universal guarantee. The optimal witnesses and the distinction between statewise, uniform, and local CP conditions materially affect what can be inferred from reset calculations, even though the proof ingredients are standard.
residual_risks: No specific trajectory or fixed point in the prior work is shown nonphysical by the uniform obstruction alone.
